_readme: Graphics and performance settings RomCrate can apply per console. 'tested: true' = checked on a real device by the project owner; everything else is a suggestion based on the emulator's own documentation and source code, and is shown as 'not tested yet'. Setting names come from each emulator's source code (see 'source'). RomCrate only changes the keys listed here, backs up any file it changes, and never touches saves, BIOS files or controls.
screens: The AYN Odin 2 Portal's screen is 1920x1080, the same as a 1080p TV, so one set of settings suits both.

override.label: Aspect ratio: 4:3
override.why: The shape a SNES picture had on a TV.

override.label: Integer scaling: off
override.why: Fills the screen height instead of leaving black borders.

profiles.source: Owner's setup session on the Odin 2 Portal (handheld spec §3.1); keys from RetroArch configuration.c / retroarch.cfg

shader_styles.label: Sharp pixels
shader_styles.why: Crisp, faithful pixels without the uneven look of plain scaling.

shader_styles.label: Smooth HD
shader_styles.why: Smooths pixel edges into clean outlines, so it looks like an HD remaster.
shader_styles.hint: Great for Donkey Kong Country, Yoshi's Island and other cartoon-style games.

shader_styles.label: CRT TV
shader_styles.why: The look the games were drawn for: blends dithering and gives richer colour. Light enough for handhelds.

shader_styles.label: CRT TV (best quality)
shader_styles.why: The most realistic CRT look. Heavier than CRT TV.
shader_styles.hint: May slow down weaker devices. Needs RetroArch's Vulkan video driver.

override.label: Aspect ratio: as the core says (Game Boy shape)
override.why: Keeps the square-ish Game Boy screen shape.

override.label: Integer scaling: on
override.why: Every pixel the same size (7× on a 1080p screen) — perfectly sharp.

profiles.source: RetroArch aspect ratio index from gfx/video_defines.h (ASPECT_RATIO_CORE = 22)

override.label: Aspect ratio: as the core says (GBA shape)
override.why: Keeps the wide GBA screen shape.

override.label: Integer scaling: on
override.why: Every pixel the same size (6× on a 1080p screen) — perfectly sharp.

profiles.source: RetroArch aspect ratio index from gfx/video_defines.h (ASPECT_RATIO_CORE = 22)

vulkan.label: Graphics plugin: ParaLLEl-RDP
vulkan.why: Fixes the black screen you get with RetroArch's Vulkan driver.

vulkan.label: Upscaling: 2×
vulkan.why: Sharper 3D; light enough for the Snapdragon 8 Gen 2.

profiles.note_if_other_driver: RetroArch uses the OpenGL driver here, which works with the N64 core's default graphics plugin — nothing to change.
profiles.source: Owner's setup session (N64 black screen fix); option names from mupen64plus-libretro-nx libretro_core_options.h

options.label: Internal resolution: 5× (1080p)
options.why: SwanStation's own setting for a 1080p screen — much sharper 3D.

set.label: Internal resolution: 2× (about 1080p)
set.why: Matches a 1080p screen; Wii/GameCube games run at full speed at 2× on the Snapdragon 8 Gen 2.

profiles.note: Wii and GameCube share these settings.
profiles.source: Dolphin Source/Core/Core/Config/GraphicsSettings.cpp and MainSettings.cpp; user folder from dolphin-emu.org 'controlling the global user directory'

set.label: Rendering resolution: 4× (1088p)
set.why: Matches a 1080p screen; PSP games are light enough for this.

profiles.source: PPSSPP Core/Config.cpp ([Graphics] GraphicsBackend written as '3 (VULKAN)'; InternalResolution)

profiles.why_checklist: ARMSX2 doesn't keep its settings in a file this computer can change yet, so here's exactly what to set.
steps: Internal Resolution: 3× (2× for heavy games like shooters and racers)
TV Shader: Off · FXAA: On · CAS: Sharpen
Auto apply widescreen 16:9 patches: On · Aspect Ratio: Auto
Only if one game needs it: long-press the game → Game Settings, and change resolution or aspect there
profiles.source: Owner's setup session on the Odin 2 Portal (handheld spec §3.1)

per_game.label: Internal resolution
per_game.step: In ARMSX2, long-press the game → Game Settings → Graphics → Internal Resolution: {label}

profiles.why_checklist: melonDS keeps its settings inside the app, so here's exactly what to set.
steps: Layout: Hybrid or side-by-side when playing with buttons; map a 'Swap screens' hotkey
On the TV, games that need touch (aiming, menus) still use the Odin's own screen — hold the Odin as the controller
Tip: 007 Quantum of Solace plays better with the Odin held upright and a custom vertical layout
profiles.source: Owner's setup session (handheld spec §3.1) and the owner's own tip

per_game_rules.why: Shooters and racers are the heaviest PS2 games; on the Odin 2 Portal they run better at 2× than 3×.
per_game_rules.source: Owner's setup session on the Odin 2 Portal (handheld spec §3.1); genre from the LaunchBox games database
